title: Geometric regularity criterion for smoothness over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Then $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] if and only if, for every finitely generated field extension $L/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] and every point $x\in X_L=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-pc-fibre-product], the local ring $\mathcal O_{X_L,x}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Here finitely generated means that $L$ is generated as a field over $k$ by finitely many elements; no perfectness, dimension, reducedness, connectedness or separatedness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 038X (lemma-geometrically-regular-smooth), pointwise equivalence at every point; Tag 038T (definition-geometrically-regular), finitely generated field extensions

proof.text: Assume f smooth. Scheme smoothness is stable under base change, so X_L is smooth over L for every field extension, without using finite generation. Around a point of X_L choose a spectrum chart Spec R. The chart map followed by the structure map is smooth, and HasRingHomProperty.Spec_iff identifies this with Algebra.Smooth L R [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine]. Its localizations are regular by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local]. Spec.stalkIso and the isomorphism on stalks of the open immersion identify this localization with the required stalk [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization].

For the converse take a spectrum chart i:Spec A -> X. Equip A with the k-algebra structure obtained from Spec.preimage(i followed by f). Local finite type gives Algebra.FiniteType k A [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A is finitely presented over the Noetherian field k [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]. For p in Spec A set K=kappa(p); essential finite type of residue fields and IntermediateField.fg_top show K/k is finitely generated [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-residue-field-extension-finitely-generated].

For every finitely generated L/k, pullbackSymmetry followed by pullbackSpecIso identifies the base-changed chart with Spec(L tensor_k A) [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Compose the inverse isomorphism with pullback.map induced by i and identity maps; Mathlib Scheme.pullback_map_isOpenImmersion makes this an open immersion into X_L. The assumed regularity of its image stalk transfers along its stalk isomorphism and Spec.stalkIso. Hence every localization of L tensor_k A at a prime is regular [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization].

Use the tensor universal property (AlgHom.liftEquiv) to construct epsilon:K tensor_k A -> K, lambda tensor a |-> lambda times residue(a) [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Its kernel q is prime. Ideal.ResidueField.lift_a extends epsilon to a K-algebra embedding kappa(q) -> K: elements outside q map to nonzero elements, hence units [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Algebraic separability descends along this embedding. Each intermediate field has the empty transcendence basis, giving IsSeparableExtension K kappa(q) [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. The tensor algebra is finite type over K and its localization at q is regular by the preceding step. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-separable-residue-smooth] yields smoothness at q.

The contraction of q under includeRight is p: epsilon(1 tensor a)=residue(a), which vanishes precisely for a in p (Ideal.algebraMap_residueField_eq_zero). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-at-prime-field-extension-descent] to deduce IsSmoothAtPrime k p. Thus there is g outside p with A_g smooth over k.

For each p take the smooth principal localization supplied by the preceding step. Mathlib Algebra.basicOpen_subset_smoothLocus_iff_smooth puts p in the algebraic smooth locus; since all primes belong, Algebra.smoothLocus_eq_univ_iff gives formal smoothness of A. Together with finite presentation this gives Algebra.Smooth k A. Transfer to the spectrum map by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine]. Apply IsZariskiLocalAtSource.iff_of_openCover to X.affineCover, using isoSpec to present each component as a spectrum. This gives Smooth f [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], including the empty scheme.
